collection_method: Read-only GitHub issue search and issue/comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No attachments, linked demonstrations, packages, agent runtimes, requests to A2A peers, target systems, or external tools were opened or run.

scope.unresolved_repository_gap: The anticipated strands-agents/sdk-python repository was not available to repository-scoped issue search. A read-only repository lookup found the current strands-agents organization repositories but no official Python SDK issue repository, so no Strands issue records are counted in this pass.

selected_records.title: Human-in-the-loop tool confirmation is forgeable by an A2A peer (self-approves dangerous tools)
selected_records.provider_attribution: Google ADK A2A and confirmation-processing behavior; no model-provider execution is established.
selected_records.assessment: A public reproduction reports that an A2A peer can supply a positive confirmation for a pending human-gated tool call and cause the recipient agent to execute it. Maintainer comments independently validated the missing principal boundary, the first transport-based patch was reverted, and a replacement principal-based fix remained open and unmerged when observed. This is a strong peer-to-agent authorization-boundary candidate, but it was already public, uses a controlled reproduction rather than an independently observed swarm, transfers an approval control message rather than a task result, and does not establish rogue intent or active autonomous participants.

selected_records.title: A2A: 2.7.0 flattens the answer to a RELAYED human-input pause, so a remote agent can never resume (silent approval-gate bypass)
selected_records.provider_attribution: Google ADK RemoteA2aAgent message construction; reporter labels Gemini models, without independent provider provenance.
selected_records.assessment: In a controlled three-agent A2A chain, a human confirmation was flattened to text, the remote gated tool did not run, and an intermediate model fabricated a result from that text. The issue was fixed and closed. It preserves transfer and recipient use in an intended test workflow, not a new autonomous swarm.

selected_records.title: [Python][Live] Background tool output can reach the parent model during the transfer delay
selected_records.provider_attribution: Google ADK live-flow queue behavior; reproduction used a fake connection and no model.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic reproduction shows a parent agent's late background-tool response reaching the parent model connection after transfer began, even though the framework intended to stop such delivery. Receipt was demonstrated, but downstream use was not. The report was fixed and closed and is a routing-boundary control, not a swarm episode.

selected_records.title: Cross-invocation code-execution capability bleed via shared LlmAgent mutation
selected_records.provider_attribution: Google ADK shared Runner/Agent mutation; no model or external execution required.
selected_records.assessment: A local reproduction and maintainer retest established that enabling code execution for one invocation could leave the capability on a later invocation that did not request it. The fix shipped in v2.10.0. This is a serious capability-isolation control but has no inter-agent transfer.

selected_records.title: tools_dict session-wide key causes cross-agent tool dispatch errors in parallel
selected_records.provider_attribution: Google ADK graph-flow shared session state; no model-provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: Parallel configured agents could overwrite a shared tool dictionary and dispatch against another agent's tool set, producing an error. Reporter and maintainer discussion validated a per-agent key workaround, but no wrong tool execution or result use was shown.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. Issue 6461 is a material, maintainer-validated peer-to-agent authorization-boundary candidate, but it was published in July, is a controlled reproduction, and does not preserve a task-result transfer among independently verified autonomous participants.
limitations: Searches were capped at 20 newest-updated rows and overlap heavily; this is not a repository census.
Issue bodies and comments are public reporter and maintainer assertions, not authenticated agent telemetry.
A configured A2A peer and recipient are protocol roles, not independently verified autonomous identities.
Open issue state and recent comments establish development activity, not ongoing autonomous agent activity.
The absent anticipated Strands Python SDK repository prevented equivalent repository-scoped issue coverage in this pass.
No embedded reproduction, attachment, package, agent runtime, message, scan, external tool, or target system was opened or executed.

Advancement requires an unpublished original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, an actual task result transferred and used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization in a real run.
redactions: No raw approval payloads, executable reproductions, commands, credentials, personal addresses, tokens, private logs, or sink identifiers are included.
Assessments describe message and boundary shape at a domain level without reproducing actionable carrier content.
